text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Zastava arms workers continue protests in Kraguajevac.
- Survey conducted by Bosnian Serb Ekstra Magazin on forthcoming elections show 50.5 percent of those polled do not know the name of the Bosnian Serb presidential candidates.

- U.S. company ICN Pharmaceuticals and Bosnian Serb company Krajinalek initial Saturday an agreement on the establishment of a limited liability pharmaceuticals company ICN-Krajinalek which will be based in Banjaluka.
- Economic results in the first eight months of this year are satisfactory, says Serbian Deputy Prime Minister Slobodan Radulovic.
- Yugoslavia should increase productivity rather than seek new investments, says director of Novi Sad center for production management Milan Nonkovic.
- Novi Sad shipbuilder completes two vessels sold to German shipowner.
- After more than three years, Yugoslavs under 26 years of age can again travel with Interrail cards.
- Montgenegrin President Momir Bulatovic leaves for a visit to the U.S.. First stop scheduled to be the U.N. in New York to discuss territorial dispute with Croatia over Prevlaka peninsula.
- Independent TV Banja Luka starts experimental transmissions with six hours of programme daily.
- Chemical industry Nevena from Leskovac signs two million german mark agreeement with packaging factory in Kumanovo, Macedonia from July 30.
- Foreign currency reserves are stable and have a tendency to grow in July and August, says Yugoslav deputy Prime Minister Jovan Zebic.
- Trepca mining and metallurgy complex advertises openings for 2,450 workers and 235 engineers.
